brief: Across 453 large-cap active mutual funds with $3.9 trillion in equity assets, 42% are beating their benchmarks YTD versus a 37% historical average. Growth funds have the highest outperformance share in a decade (81%) despite weak absolute returns, while value funds posted the best absolute YTD return (14%) but only 4% beat their benchmark. Cash balances are 1.1% of assets, matching the December 2025 record low. Active equity mutual funds saw about $350 billion of YTD outflows, a 12th straight year of outflows, while US equity ETFs took in about $960 billion, $210 billion of it since the start of Q4. Funds remain underweight AI-exposed equities, but the underweight narrowed to 130bp from 175bp, with AMD, WDC, STX, SNDK, PLTR, SNOW, TWLO, PANW and CRWD among the most popular increases and AMAT, LRCX, CSCO and KLAC among the most popular decreases. Funds stayed 722bp underweight the Magnificent 7, unchanged on the quarter. AMZN turned to an average overweight for the first time since 2016, while GOOGL and AAPL saw the largest ownership cuts. High return dispersion and improving market breadth have supported fund returns. Sector tilts: most overweight Industrials, Health Care (a 10-year high) and Financials, most underweight Info Tech.
